title: Tech Note: Date Entry
author: Elaine Smith
featured_technology: On Before Keystroke / On After Keystroke form events
HandleDate / StringToDate example methods (Tom Dillon, DataCraft)
SET DEFAULT CENTURY for two-digit year resolution

historical_commentary.text: Elaine Smith (Technical Support Engineer) demonstrates trapping keystrokes with the On Before Keystroke form event and the FILTER KEYSTROKE/Keystroke commands to let users type single-letter shortcuts (T, M, H, Y, R, +, -) into a date field to jump to today, month/year boundaries, or adjust the date by a day, using Tom Dillon's HandleDate/StringToDate example methods. The general capability (trap and reinterpret keystrokes in a field) is still fully supported and used in modern 4D applications, but this specific hidden function-key-driven date shortcut UI reflects a 2001-era paradigm; most current 4D interfaces favor discoverable calendar picker widgets over undocumented single-letter shortcuts, so the technique itself is now largely obsolete even though the underlying keystroke-trapping commands remain unchanged.
related_updates: 4D form objects now commonly use built-in date/calendar picker controls rather than custom function-key-driven entry routines
The On Before Keystroke/On After Keystroke events and FILTER KEYSTROKE/Keystroke commands described remain part of the current 4D language, unchanged in behavior
Modern UI/UX conventions favor discoverable calendar widgets over hidden function-key shortcuts
